claim.statement: A fresh-process Darwin probe materializes the four pinned real DINOv3 embedding roles within the existing 16 MiB caller budget and reports positive managed-allocation/live-heap/RSS orientation without running the encoder.
claim.scope: One user-local safetensors artifact, four embedding roles, one CPU process, and post-GC orientation only; no true peak, native allocator, forward, block, GPU, or Metal claim.

evidence.result: 1 example, 0 failures; 16 MiB retained control moved post-GC managed heap by 16863232 bytes and ps RSS by 16512 KiB
existing caller budget guard rejects before role payload materialization

dod: The probe requires an explicit user-local checkpoint path and Darwin compilation flag.
The pinned file size, four-role F32 byte count, and role payload digest are checked.
A qualified 16 MiB control demonstrates that the managed/RSS sensor can detect a known positive allocation.
The probe emits cumulative allocation and post-GC live/RSS orientation while marking forward, native peak, and Metal as unrun or unmeasured.

excluded: peak/high-water memory during digest or role decode

residual_risks: ps RSS is a local process-resident orientation and is unavailable in the restricted sandbox without escalation.
Post-GC live-heap values are conservative and may retain stale roots; the dropped value is diagnostic, not a release guarantee.
The one-run fixed-artifact result does not establish a true peak, native allocator, latency, or production memory budget.
The real embedding forward remains rejected by the existing multiply-add policy, and no model block or Metal code ran.
